name: felinks
desc: Text mode browser and Gemini, NNTP, FTP, Gopher, Finger, and BitTorrent client
why: A text-mode browser that also speaks Gemini, Gopher, Finger and NNTP, a fun way back into older internet protocols.

brief.what_it_is: ELinks is a text-mode web browser that runs in a terminal. The README describes it as a feature-rich browser for HTTP and FTP that can render frames and tables, is customizable, and can be extended with scripts. This package, felinks, is a fork of ELinks maintained by rkd77. The README does not list Gemini, Gopher, NNTP, Finger, or BitTorrent support, though the scout notes claim them. Those protocol claims are unverified in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The README's history section says ELinks began as a development version of Links, a Lynx-like text browser, to offer more liberal feature policies and a fuller-featured alternative that is still stable. The felinks fork exists because the old ELinks team lost interest, and the fork continues development from the master branch of the original repo.
brief.install_notes: The README points to an INSTALL file for build instructions and a SITES file for mirrors, but I did not fetch either. Nothing in the README mentions a runtime, account, or first-run configuration. The brew package is named felinks and its executable is elinks.
brief.standout: The fork's README states a release policy: main releases no more often than once a year, and bugfix point releases no more often than monthly. The README also describes the project's modular design, with cookies, bookmarks, SSL, and scripting kept as separate add-on modules to limit bloat.
brief.status: unknown. The README gives release-cadence rules for felinks but no release dates, last commit date, or version number. It says the repo was renamed to elinks on 2020-12-01. The felinks repo URL I fetched returned identical content, so it does not add evidence.
brief.caveats: The homepage README is for ELinks and does not mention the protocols in the scout notes (Gemini, Gopher, NNTP, Finger, BitTorrent). Those claims need checking against the docs or the source before the entry says them. The homepage link goes to the elinks repo, not a felinks-specific one. I did not check the INSTALL file, so build requirements are unknown.
quotes: ELinks is an advanced and well-established feature-rich text mode web (HTTP/FTP/..) browser.

felinks (fork of elinks) is continuation of elinks based on the master branch of the original elinks repo with main releases (new features and other incompatible changes) no more often than 1 yearly, and point releases (bugfixes) no more often than once a month.
ELinks, on the contrary, aims to provide a full-featured web browser, superior to both lynx and w3m and with the power (but not slowness and memory usage) of Mozilla, Konqueror and similar browsers.
